sentences.text: Santosh Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April,

2024 
Author: Chief Justice
Bench: Chief Justice
 1
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur
Cra No. 5676 of 2023

(Santosh Lodhi Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh And
 Dated : 16-04-2024

Shri P.S. Chouhan - Advocate for appellant.
 Shri Pramod Thakre - Public Prosecutor for respondents/S
Heard on I.A. No.15138 of 2023.
2.

This is the first application seeking for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant-accused - Santosh Lodhi, who has been convicted under Section 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for life and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/- and further convicted under Section 323 of IPC r/w Section 3(2)(va) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for three months and to pay fine of Rs.500/- and also sentenced under Section 506 (Part-II) of IPC r/w 3(2)(va) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for two years and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/-
respectively with default stipulations as mentioned in the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 22.02.2023 passed by the Special Judge, POCSO Act, District Chhatarpur in Special Case No.103 of 2021.
3. The case of the prosecution is that on 12.05.2021 at about 4.00 PM when the prosecutrix went to attend the nature's call, the appellant came over there, caught hold her and committed rape with her.
The prosecutrix went home and narrated the incident to her sister and brother-in-law.
On 13.05.2021, she went to police station Bandha and lodged the report against the appellant.
Her statement was recorded wherein she alleged against the present appellant for commission of offences as aforementioned.
The appellant was arrested on 17.05.2021.
After trial, the appellant was convicted and sentenced as mentioned above.
4. This application has been filed on the ground that appellant and the prosecutrix were known to each other and hence it appears that she was a consenting party.
There is no likelihood of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
The appellant is in jail since 17.05.2021.
He is ready to abide by Santosh Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024

all the terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court while considering the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
5. P e r contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the contentions stating therein that the prosecutrix was minor aged about 16 years at the time of commission of offence.
He has categorically opposed the manner in which the offence has taken place.
The DNA profile is found to be positive.
There is no explanation of the same that could be given by the appellant.
The prosecutrix has supported the prosecution story.
In view of the aforesaid, he has prayed for rejection of the application.

6. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, the age of the victim coupled with the manner in which the offence has been committed, this Court does not deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
7. Accordingly, I.A. No.15138 of 2023 is rejected.
(RAVI MALIMATH) (V
